chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The pebbles for throwing at the Jamarat: if you take them from the Haram (sanctuary), it will suffice you; and if you take them from outside the Haram, it will not suffice you.
He said, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not throw the Jamarat except with pebbles.'
And the smooth (pebbles) from the pebbles are disliked, and the rough (pebbles) from them are recommended. He narrated.

key_terms.حَصَى الْجِمَارِ: Pebbles for throwing at the Jamarat pillars

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for the validity of pebbles used in Ramy al-Jamarat according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the validity of the pebbles used in *Ramy al-Jamarat* by linking their ritual efficacy to their origin within the sacred precincts of Mecca (*Haram*), a distinction emphasized by Shia jurists to ensure the physical components of the rite are ritually pure. It further refines the practice by discouraging the use of smooth pebbels (*al-summ*) in favor of rough ones (*al-bursh*), ensuring the pebbles are thrown effectively rather than merely dropped, thereby fulfilling the spirit of the act of casting. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on both the spatial sanctity and the physical quality of ritual instruments.
